chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We are the origin of every good, and from our branches is every righteousness; so from the righteousness are: monotheism, prayer, fasting, suppressing anger, pardoning the wrongdoer, showing mercy to the poor, attending to the neighbor, and acknowledging the superiority of the deserving ones.

And our enemy is the origin of every evil, and from their branches is every ugliness and immorality; so from them are: lying, stinginess, slander, cutting off relations, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of the orphan without right, exceeding the limits which Allah commanded, committing indecencies, both apparent and hidden, adultery, theft, and everything consistent with that from the ugly.
He has lied who claims to be with us while he is attached to the branches of others.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of true followers of the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the theological principle of 'Usul al-Khayr' (the Root of All Good), positing that the Ahl al-Bayt are the ontological source from which all virtues like monotheism and prayer emanate, while their enemies are the source of all vices. By linking specific moral practices to the Ahl al-Bayt, it underscores their role as the living embodiment of divine guidance, a concept central to Shia cosmology and jurisprudence. The conclusion serves as a criterion for authentic affiliation, distinguishing true followers from those who merely claim lineage or association while engaging in the 'fruits' of their enemies' evil.

en.hubeali: H 14784 – Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammaad, from Ibn Muskaan, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said;

‘We<sup>asws</sup> are the origin of every good, and from our<sup>asws</sup> branches is every righteousness, So, from the righteousness is ‘التَّوْحِيدُ’ Oneness (Al-Tauheed), and the Prayer, and the Fasts, and suppression of the anger, and the pardoning others, and being merciful to the poor, and being helpful to the neighbour, and accepting the preference of the deserving ones.

And our<sup>asws</sup> enemies are the origin of every evil, and from their branches is every ugliness and immorality. So, from these is the lie, and the niggardliness, and the slander, and the cutting-off (relationships), and consumption of the interest, and consumption of the wealth of the orphans without right, and infringement of the limits of the Commands of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, commission of the immoral acts, the apparent from it as well as the hidden, and the adultery, and the theft, and every that which is consistent with that from the ugliness.
So he has lied, the one who thinks he is with us<sup>asws</sup> whilst he attaches himself to the branches of others (which are) rather than ours<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 337. Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammaad, from Ibn Muskaan, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said; ‘

We (a.s.) are the origin of every good, and from our (a.s.) branches is every righteousness, So, from the righteousness is ‘التَّوْحِيدُ’ Oneness (Al-Tauheed), and the Prayer, and the Fasts, and suppression of the anger, and the pardoning others, and being merciful to the poor, and being helpful to the neighbour, and accepting the preference of the deserving ones.

And our (a.s.) enemies are the origin of every evil, and from their branches is every ugliness and immorality. So, from these is the lie, and the niggardliness, and the slander, and the cutting-off (relationships), and consumption of the interest, and consumption of the wealth of the orphans without right, and infringement of the limits of the Commands of Allah (azwj), commission of the immoral acts, the apparent from it as well as the hidden, and the adultery, and the theft, and every that which is consistent with that from the ugliness.
So he has lied, the one who thinks he is with us (a.s.) whilst he attaches himself to the branches of others (which are) rather than ours (a.s.)’.
